title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 4th District
area: South-central Tennessee, including Murfreesboro's southern exurbs, Tullahoma, and Fayetteville

context.text: Incumbent Scott DesJarlais (R) defeated Thomas Davis, Harold Jones, and Joshua James in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Victoria Broderick won a contested Democratic primary over Mike Cortese, Cliff Huffman, Tim Lanier, and Joyce Neal. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+11, and forecasters rate the general election Safe/Solid Republican. After the 2026 filing deadline reopened following Tennessee's new congressional map, the 4th District drew nine candidates in total, tied with the 6th District for the most of any Tennessee district.

candidates.name: Scott DesJarlais
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Scott DesJarlais is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 4th District, a physician who has served in the House since 2011 and chairs the Armed Services Committee's Strategic Forces Subcommittee. He is seeking re-election after winning the August 6, 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1964 and raised in Sturgis, South Dakota.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1987) and an M.D. (1991) from the University of South Dakota; his official biography says his undergraduate degrees were in chemistry and psychology.
Moved to East Tennessee in 1993 to practice medicine as a generalist and worked as a physician before being elected to Congress.
Won election to the U.S. House on November 2, 2010, defeating Democrat Lincoln Davis; his official biography says he is serving his eighth term.
Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the House Committee on Armed Services; at the start of the 119th Congress he was named chairman of the Armed Services Strategic Forces Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he is a member of the House Freedom Caucus, the GOP Doctors Caucus and the Border Security Caucus.
His legislation allowing members of the military to carry firearms at recruiting stations, introduced after the 2015 Chattanooga attack, became law in 2016, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Amy have three children and attend Epiphany Episcopal Church in Sherwood, Tennessee, where Amy grew up.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (2025-2026), including its Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture and Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry subcommittees.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (2025-2026), chairing the Subcommittee on Strategic Forces and also sitting on the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee.

candidates.name: Victoria Broderick
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested August 6, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Victoria Broderick is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 4th District, a technology-industry worker and mother of two who describes herself as becoming politically active in 2021 after the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. She chaired her local county Democratic Party, ran against Rep. Scott DesJarlais in 2024, and won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary.

background.text: Born in Tampa, Florida; her campaign website says she grew up across the South, from Atlanta to Dallas, before settling in Lincoln County, Tennessee.
Graduated from Lincoln County High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Austin Peay State University in 2015.
Works in the technology industry; Ballotpedia lists her career experience as a technology professional and sourcing coordinator, and she says she works full-time in tech while campaigning.

Says she began her political involvement in 2021 and became her local county Democratic Party chair after the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade during her maternity leave; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the Lincoln County Democrats and the Tennessee Democratic Party Executive Committee.

Was the Democratic nominee against Rep. Scott DesJarlais in the November 5, 2024 general election, which DesJarlais won; her campaign website says she built that campaign in five months while working full time after learning DesJarlais would otherwise run unopposed.
Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary for the 4th District, defeating Mike Cortese, Joyce Neal, Tim Lanier and Cliff Huffman.
Describes herself as a mother of two young boys who fosters animals with her local humane society; Ballotpedia lists an affiliation with the Lincoln County Humane Society.

priorities.text: Lists safety, affordability, and freedom as her core campaign themes.

positions.summary: Says her political involvement began after the overturning of Roe v. Wade while she was navigating a personal pregnancy experience, and lists 'freedom' among her core campaign themes.
positions.quote: Roe was overtuned during my maternity leave, and I sprang into action.

summary.text: Jacob Anders is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 4th District who describes himself as a historian, author and digital ethics researcher. He was disqualified from the 2026 Democratic primary and is on the November ballot as an independent, running on economic security in the face of AI and automation, and opposition to foreign wars.

background.text: Born in Huntsville, Alabama, and graduated from Huntsville High School.
Says he studied psychology at the University of Alabama in Huntsville and earned a bachelor's degree from Hiwassee College in 2016.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as author, historian, voice actor and political activist; he describes himself as a historian, author, voice actor and digital ethics researcher.
Says he previously volunteered for the Ron Paul, Bernie Sanders and Andrew Yang presidential campaigns.
Ballotpedia reports he was disqualified from the 2026 Democratic primary for Tennessee's 4th District and did not appear on that ballot; he is now an independent candidate in the general election.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on protecting workers and wages from AI and automation, and supports universal basic income and digital rights protections.

summary.text: Clay Faircloth is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 4th District. Ballotpedia lists his profession as pastor and social worker, and in a 2024 Candidate Connection survey he described himself as a counselor, pastor and community engagement influencer; he previously sought the Democratic nomination in the 6th District in 2022 and 2024.

background.text: Graduated from McGavock High School and earned a graduate degree from Trevecca Nazarene University in 2013.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as pastor, work at a Nissan plant, and career coaching with Metro Nashville; it lists his profession as pastor and social worker.
In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, describes himself as a counselor, pastor and community engagement influencer.

Appeared on the Democratic primary ballot for Tennessee's 6th District in 2022 and 2024, losing to Randal Cooper and Lore Bergman respectively; he is running as an independent in the 4th District in 2026.
